question: Canadair planes: why has Brussels failed to purchase any for 10 years, when it has managed to find EUR 27 million in four months to upgrade sewers in Seychelles?

France saw that its fleet of firefighting aircraft needed upgrading back in 20031. In 2017, after the fires in Portugal in 2016, the Commission noted that ‘the entire French fleet of forest fire fighting planes ... was out of service’2. At that juncture, Emmanuel Macron announced that a European force3 of around 20 Canadair-type water bombers would be in place by 2022.

Almost 10 years on, those planes were very much missed this summer. The EU is providing funding to the tune of EUR 600 million to kick-start the manufacture of 12 new planes in Canada, but they will not be ready for delivery until 2029-2030.

The European Court of Auditors has reported that ‘although there have been efforts to purchase rescEU reserves jointly, we found that these efforts had produced results in only one case4’. By way of comparison, EUR 27 million in EU funding was authorised in four months for sewers in Seychelles (a European Investment Bank loan made in 2011).
The French Development Agency provided a loan of EUR 10 million and the Commission provided a EUR 7 million grant5. 1.
Why is the funding procedure quicker when it comes to sewers in Seychelles than it is for Canadair planes in Europe?
What is the Commission going to do to speed up the delivery of Canadair planes?
Why did it not make the development of a European water bomber a priority?
